clinician.final_diagnosis: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis complicated by posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year-old male presented with 7 days of fever, headache, projectile emesis, 24-hour blurry vision, and two episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures with postictal confusion. Examination revealed severe hypertension (BP 150/100 mmHg, 99th percentile). Laboratory investigations showed elevated ASO titers, decreased complement C3, uremia, hematuria, and proteinuria, consistent with post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis. MRI brain demonstrated symmetrical enhancement of superficial and deep watershed areas predominantly in occipital and temporal regions, consistent with PRES. The patient was treated with ceftriaxone and amlodipine. Six days after admission, he was asymptomatic with minimal residual hematuria. Repeat MRI at three weeks showed complete resolution of hyperintense lesions, confirming the reversible nature of PRES.

Renal involvement with uremia, hematuria, and proteinuria confirming glomerulonephritis
MRI findings consistent with PRES: symmetrical enhancement of watershed areas in occipital and temporal regions
Treatment with ceftriaxone for antimicrobial coverage and amlodipine for blood pressure management
Clinical improvement with patient becoming asymptomatic by day 6 with minimal residual hematuria
Radiological confirmation of reversibility: complete resolution of hyperintense lesions on repeat MRI at three weeks
